migration.title: Delete publication ceremony; keep researcher-facing ontology lookup
migration.status: Plan only. No source files listed below are claimed deleted by this document.

principles.item: Deliver working XML lookup before deleting runtime dependencies.
Preserve existing published wheel/tag behavior; compatibility does not force new XML mapping authors into historical release mechanics.
Prefer removing modules and checks to building adapters around them.
Each implementation PR must show user-facing lookup improvement or an actual reduction in code/tests/workflows. Avoid one PR per file and avoid a new metadata migration program.
Do not reproduce archived JSON/coverage snapshots as generated committed XML clones.

phase.name: Freeze old release machinery
phase.action: Adopt the XML contract; mark ADR-001 and protected handoff/release architecture as superseded.
Stop opening work to harden digests, attestation, locks, release overlays or new issue-specific CI.
Continue semantic research and mapping work in batches, without manufacturing new per-batch versions.
phase.done: Only one document defines the new contribution contract; historical workflows no longer set feature-development priorities.

phase.name: Implement one working XML path
phase.action: Add stdlib ElementTree reader for src/tfont/mappings/*.xml with filename-based discovery and actionable parse errors.
Add in-memory forward and inverse indexes; implement native-to-target and corpus-to-corpus lookup for value/node mappings first.
Demonstrate two actual checked corpora (BHSA and Syriac, OLiA Noun), including reverse lookup and explicit non-identity of words.
Package the same XML files in a wheel and test the wheel rather than a checkout-only loader.
phase.done: A scholar can install ontoTF and resolve a supported BHSA category in Syriac directly from XML, without touching JSON release artifacts.

phase.name: Migrate semantic content, not ceremony
phase.action: Translate supported existing mappings to per-corpus XML, retaining target relations and relevant source links; native-only and ambiguous decisions remain explicit when useful.
Extend selector execution only as real current data requires (features, TF edge types, entity identifiers), testing each new kind with real TF behavior.
Give new corpora and ontology models the same one-file discovery path, without a release registry update or custom loader branch.
Ensure missing/unknown target, conflicting mappings, source-version mismatch, approximate direction and entity-vs-class distinction have regression tests.
phase.done: New substantive mappings require edits to one corpus XML and can be used immediately by the new default loader.

phase.name: Delete obsolete machinery by dependency
phase.action: Switch default public lookup to XML and update CLI/package/docs to the new interface. Preserve a small historical compatibility adapter only where an actually used public API requires it.
Remove protected batch reviewer workflow and per-issue overlapping workflows after replacing any genuinely unique tests in the single CI owner.
Remove handoff, attestation, packet, batch-publication and overlay modules once callers and tests have been moved to the XML path.

Delete duplicated versioned resource trees, release catalogs, batch-pilot JSON and copied coverage snapshots from the active package once the new runtime no longer imports them. Git history and released wheels preserve historical artifacts.
Remove old CI tests that require obsolete workflows or release mechanisms to exist, replacing them only with user-facing XML acceptance tests.
phase.done: One canonical XML catalog per corpus, one loader/resolver, one CI path; no legacy publisher on the default lookup path.

phase.name: Researcher E2E and contribution test
phase.action: Have an independent adversarial pass map a native BHSA selector to Syriac and back, including a false-equivalence counterexample.
Simulate an external author adding a new corpus with exactly one XML file; verify wheel installation and discovery with no Python edits.
Report actual categories and entity IDs resolvable between corpora, and distinguish these from reviewed-but-unmapped native annotations.
phase.done: Documented one-file submission succeeds and the end-to-end researcher query works on accessible real corpora.

group.name: Duplicated checks and paperwork
group.path: docs/research/ and docs/plans/ documents created solely for obsolete release ceremonies
tests that assert a retired workflow or review receipt must exist

retentions.component: Native Text-Fabric execution; simplify plans only when behavior is preserved.
Actual lookup logic; remove needless fingerprints/release coupling after XML parity.
Useful semantic types/indexes; simplify instead of generating complex bundle graph.
Existing loaded TF observation when useful to execute selectors.
Optional original permissively distributable ontology sources/evidence; RDF/XML OWL allowed, no JSON term locks needed for routine lookup.
Python packaging; include XML resources without creating copied source-of-truth files in Git.
Single nonduplicated CI owner, or replace with a simpler single CI workflow.
One authoritative corpus XML file per corpus, plus one shared basic schema.
Existing published releases remain available as Git tags/wheels; no retroactive rewriting or cryptographic verification requirement.

stop-rules.rule: Do not create a replacement attestation layer, certificate, digest registry, release lock catalog or review-ticket hierarchy.
Do not require schema version increments for ordinary mapping additions.
Do not block useful category lookup on unrelated ontology imports, CI refactors or complete corpus inventory accounting.
Do not add fake example mappings to production; examples must remain clearly nonauthoritative until checked against actual corpus data.
Do not delete a module before checking its active imports and preserving truly user-facing behavior; the end state should have less code than the starting state.
